Ready. Press \"Scan again\" and put the remote in pairing mode.
This device has no Bluetooth adapter.
Scanning for 30 seconds. A recognized remote is paired automatically; otherwise select it on the right. The strongest signal (closest to 0 dBm) is usually the remote.
Location is off: Fire OS 8 returns no scan results without it.
Scan finished. Select your remote on the right, or scan again.
The pairing request for %1$s was rejected. Scan again to retry.
Pairing with %1$s failed. Put the remote in pairing mode and scan again.
Pair Remote: volume buttons to TV

Keeps Pair Remote running in the background. Volume key presses are read from the Fire OS system log and sent to the TV over the network, because Fire OS ignores them on HDMI. No screen content is read and no keys are filtered.
Press \"Find TV\" to search the network.
Working. Volume buttons on Bluetooth remotes change the TV volume.
Almost done: log access (step 6 on the right) is missing.
Not set up yet. Follow the steps on the right.
Settings → System → About → click \"Android TV OS build\" 7 times. Then Developer options → USB debugging: on.
Select the TV on the left, press \"Save & test\", and on the TV choose Always allow → Allow.
ON THIS FIRE TV, FROM A COMPUTER
Settings → My Fire TV → Developer options → ADB debugging: on.
On the computer, open Command Prompt in the folder with adb.exe and connect. If this screen asks to allow USB debugging, choose Always allow → OK.
Turn on the background service. The command keeps the services that are already on:
Type the commands exactly as shown. After the last one the app restarts once by itself. In Git Bash, write the adb path with forward slashes (/c/adb/adb).
No TV selected yet. Searching the network…
Enter an IP address such as 192.168.1.28, or 192.168.1.28:5555.
Connecting to %1$s…\nIf the TV asks \"Allow debugging?\", choose Always allow → Allow.
Could not connect to %1$s: %2$s\nCheck that the TV is on and USB debugging is enabled, then press \"Save & test\" again.
No device with ADB debugging found. Turn on USB debugging on the TV, or type its IP address.
